name: Vermont
sources: Vermont GB-1210 2026 withholding tables (tax.vermont.gov/sites/tax/files/documents/GB-1210-2026.pdf): single and married 2026 bracket thresholds

Vermont Joint Fiscal Office, House Ways and Means testimony 4-23-2026 (legislature.vermont.gov, DR 26-0804): current-law TY2026 brackets for all four statuses; Tax Department presentation 4-15-2026: top bracket $312,050 joint for TY26
Vermont IN-111 2025 and instructions (tax.vermont.gov): standard deduction $7,650/$15,300/$11,450, $1,250 per 65+/blind box, $5,300 personal exemption
Vermont Schedule IN-153 2025: flat exclusion = lesser of net capital gain or $5,000; 40% exclusion excludes publicly traded stocks and bonds
provisional: Standard deduction ($7,650 single and separate, $15,300 joint, $11,450 head of household) and the $1,250 extra per person 65+ are 2025 amounts; 2026 indexed amounts are not yet published.
Personal exemption $5,300 is the 2025 amount (the 2026 withholding allowance is $5,400).
2026 brackets for head of household and married filing separately come from the Joint Fiscal Office; the Department's 2026 rate schedules are not yet published.
notes: Vermont's charitable contribution credit (5% of gifts, up to $1,000) is not included.
Only the flat $5,000 capital gains exclusion is applied; the 40% exclusion for non-traded assets held over three years (such as a business or land) is not included.
